summary: Leslie proves the endoscopic fundamental lemma for the infinitesimal symmetric space of U(2n)/U(n) × U(n), the first step in stabilizing the (unstable) relative trace formula of unitary Friedberg–Jacquet periods ∫_{[U(W_1)×U(W_2)]}φ (Conjecture 1.1, a case of Getz–Wambach): for E/F unramified, 1_{End(Λ_n)} and 1_{End(Λ_a)} ⊗ 1_{End(Λ_b)} are smooth transfers for the relative endoscopic datum (a, b) (Theorem 2.12 = Theorem 1.3). Part 1 reduces this, by the contraction map End(V_n) → Herm(V_n) and Hironaka's spherical Hecke module of the Hermitian symmetric variety X_n, to an endoscopic fundamental lemma for that Hecke module (Theorem 3.5), then, by Xiao's germ expansion relating κ-orbital integrals to Jacquet–Rallis nilpotent orbital integrals and by Beuzart-Plessis's Weil representation on orbital integrals, to a Jacquet–Rallis transfer statement for BC(φ) and φ ∗ 1_0 (Theorem 5.3). Part 2 proves that statement by a new 'twisted Jacquet–Rallis' comparison of simple relative trace formulas (Res_{E/F}(GL_n × GL_{n+1}) with U(V_x) × U(V_y) against GL_n × GL_{n+1} with GL_n), using Feigon–Lapid–Offen's unitary periods, and deduces a base change fundamental lemma for the spherical Hecke algebra (Theorem 11.1). The atlas plans unitary endoscopy (ET.0–ET.3) but not endoscopy for symmetric spaces, so Part 1 becomes a new Part II of EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison; the twisted comparison coalesces with the pending Jacquet–Rallis Part II; unitary endoscopic computations, Satake/Hall–Littlewood facts, Hermitian lattices and densities, and Ramakrishnan's theorem go to ET.0–ET.1, SR.4, GN.2–GN.3 and AL.3. Twelve misprints are recorded.

items.name: Haar measure normalizations (after Feigon–Lapid–Offen)
items.statement: For a local field F, an additive character ψ and a non-singular variety Y of dimension d with gauge form ω_Y, dy = c(ψ)^{d/2} λ_Y dy^Tam, where c(ψ) = q^m if cond(ψ) = ϖ^m O_F (nonarchimedean) and |a|_F if ψ(x) = e^{2πi Tr_{E/ℝ}(ax)}; ω_{Res_{E/F} Y} = p_*(ω_Y); ω_{GL_n} = ∏dg_{ij}/det(g)^n with λ_{GL_n} = ∏_{i=1}^n L(i, 1_{F^×}) (and λ_{Res GL_n} = ∏ L(i, 1_{E^×})); ω_N = ∏dx_i, λ_N = 1 for unipotent N; ω_{X_n} = ∏_{i≤j}dx_{ij}/det(x)^n with λ_{X_n} = ∏ L(i, η^{i+1}); ω_{U(V)} compatible with these and λ_{U(V)} = ∏ L(i, η^i), so that X_n ≅ ⊔_{x∈𝒱_n} GL_n(E)/U(V_x) is measure-compatible. For ψ of conductor O_F, K_n = GL_n(O_F), and for E/F unramified K_{n,E} = GL_n(O_E) and X_n(O_F) = GL_n(O_E) ∗ I_n, have volume 1. On the centralizer T_δ of a regular semisimple δ ∈ Herm(V) the measure gives its maximal compact subgroup volume 1.
items.note: AA.2 plans Tamagawa measures from invariant differential forms and convergence factors; these are the paper's specific constants (following [FLO12]), used in the unit-volume statements of Part 1 and in the volume identities vol([Z_{H′_{x,y}}]) = (2L(1, η))² of Part 2.

items.name: Lemma 1.8 (centralizers and cohomology of regular semisimple Hermitian elements)
items.statement: Let δ ∈ Herm(V) be regular semisimple, F[δ] = F[X]/(char_δ) = ∏_{i=1}^m F_i with F_i/F fields, E_i = E ⊗_F F_i and S_1 = {i : F_i ⊉ E}, so that E[δ] = ∏_{S_1} E_i × ∏_{S_2} F_i ⊕ F_i. Then the centralizer T_δ of δ in U(V) satisfies T_δ ≅ Z_{U(V)}(F) E[δ]^×/F[δ]^×, H^1(F, T_δ) = ∏_{S_1} ℤ/2ℤ, and C(T_δ/F) = ker(H^1(F, T_δ) → H^1_ab(F, U(V))) = ker(∏_{S_1} ℤ/2ℤ → ℤ/2ℤ), the map being the sum of the factors. The unique maximal compact subgroup is T_{S_1} ≅ Z_{U(V)}(F) ∏_{S_1} E_i^×/F_i^× × ∏_{S_2} O_{F_i}^×.
items.note: Proved by citation of Rogawski [Rog90, 3.4]. The statement prints 'centralizer of δ in U(W)'; U(V) is meant (sourceIssues E1). Uses Kottwitz–Borovoi abelianized cohomology (ET.0).

items.name: The infinitesimal symmetric pair (U(W_1) × U(W_2), 𝔲(W)_1)
items.statement: For n-dimensional Hermitian spaces W_1, W_2 over E and W = W_1 ⊕ W_2 with involution ε(w_1 + w_2) = w_1 − w_2, the Lie algebra 𝔲(W) = 𝔲(W)_0 ⊕ 𝔲(W)_1 is ℤ/2-graded with 𝔲(W)_0 = 𝔲(W_1) ⊕ 𝔲(W_2) and 𝔲(W)_1 = Hom_E(W_2, W_1) (the tangent space of Q = U(W)/U(W_1) × U(W_2)); U(W_1) × U(W_2) acts by (g, h)·φ = g ∘ φ ∘ h^{-1}. Every δ ∈ 𝔲(W)_1 is δ(X) = (0, X; −X^τ, 0) with ⟨Xw_2, w_1⟩_1 = ⟨w_2, X^τ w_1⟩_2; H_δ = {(h, g) : h^{-1}δg = δ} is its stabilizer. The regular semisimple locus 𝔲(W)_1^rss (closed orbit of maximal dimension) equals 𝔲(W)_1 ∩ 𝔲(W)^rss, since the pair is geometrically quasi-split [Les21, §1.2]; for δ regular semisimple H_δ is a torus of rank n.
items.note: The relative (symmetric-space) analogue of the adjoint action on a Lie algebra.

items.name: The contraction maps r_1, r_2
items.statement: r_i : 𝔲(W)_1 → Herm(W_i) with r_1(δ(X)) = −XX^τ and r_2(δ(X)) = −X^τX (2.1). For W_1 = W_2 = V_n, 𝔲(W)_1 = End(V_n) and r = r_1 is the contraction map r_n : End(V_n) → Herm(V_n) of [Les19].

items.name: Proposition 2.1 (the contraction map is a categorical quotient)
items.statement: The map r = r_1 intertwines the U(W_1)-action on 𝔲(W)_1 and the adjoint action on Herm(W_1), and (Herm(W_1), r) is a categorical quotient for the U(W_2)-action on 𝔲(W)_1.
items.note: Proof over F̄ with GL_n × GL_n acting on gl_n × gl_n, r(X, Y) = XY, via Igusa's criterion [Zha14b, §3] (codimension-two complement of the image, generic fibres a single orbit).

items.name: Lemma 2.2 (invariant quotient of 𝔲(W)_1)
items.statement: Let π : 𝔲(W)_1 → 𝔸^n send δ(X) to the coefficients of the characteristic polynomial of r(δ(X)) = −XX^τ. Then (𝔸^n, π) is a categorical quotient for the U(W_1) × U(W_2)-action on 𝔲(W)_1.
items.note: Same argument as Proposition 2.1.

items.name: Lemma 2.3 (the contraction on the non-singular locus is a torsor)
items.statement: On 𝔲(W)_1^iso ≅ Iso_E(W_2, W_1), r is an algebraic U(W_2)-torsor; for δ ∈ 𝔲(W)_1^iso, (h_1, h_2) ↦ h_1 is an isomorphism φ_δ : H_δ ≅ T_{r(δ)} onto the centralizer of r(δ) in U(W_1), and φ_δ induces D(H_δ/F) ≅ D(T_{r(δ)}/F), where D(H_δ/F) = ker(H^1(F, H_δ) → H^1(F, U(W_1) × U(W_2))) and D(T_{r(δ)}/F) = ker(H^1(F, T_{r(δ)}) → H^1(F, U(W_1))) (2.2). Hence rational U(W_1) × U(W_2)-orbits in the stable orbit of δ correspond to rational conjugacy classes in the stable class of r(δ).
items.note: Proof cited from [Les19, Lemma 3.9] and [Les22, Lemma 5.12].

items.name: Relative orbital integrals on 𝔲(W)_1
items.statement: For f ∈ C_c^∞(𝔲(W)_1) and δ ∈ 𝔲(W)_1 semisimple, RO(f, δ) = ∫_{H_δ\U(W_1)×U(W_2)} f(h_1^{-1}δh_2) dh_1 dh_2 (2.3).

items.name: Lemma 2.4 (regular semisimple elements are non-singular)
items.statement: 𝔲(W)_1^rss ⊂ 𝔲(W)_1^iso.
items.note: Over F̄, (X, Y) is regular semisimple iff Z = (0, X; Y, 0) ∈ gl_{2n} is, and π(X, Y)(t²) = det(tI_{2n} − Z).

items.name: The pushforward r_! along the contraction
items.statement: With Ω = r(𝔲(W)_1^iso) and Ω_reg = r(𝔲(W)_1^rss), r : 𝔲(W)_1^iso → Ω is a submersion; for f ∈ C_c^∞(𝔲(W)_1^iso) and x regular semisimple, r_!(f)(r(x)) = ∫_{U(W_2)} f(xu) du (2.4) converges and lies in C_c^∞(Ω), and r_! : C_c^∞(𝔲(W)_1^iso) → C_c^∞(Ω) and C_c^∞(𝔲(W)_1^rss) → C_c^∞(Ω_reg) are surjective.
items.note: Surjectivity is Harish-Chandra's submersion principle as in Shalika [Sha72, §1].

items.name: Lemma 2.5 (relative orbital integrals as twisted-Lie-algebra orbital integrals)
items.statement: For f ∈ C_c^∞(𝔲(W)_1) and x ∈ 𝔲(W)_1^rss, RO(f, x) converges and RO(f, x) = ∫_{T_{r(x)}\U(W_1)} r_!(f)(g^{-1}r(x)g) dg = Orb(r_!(f), r(x)), after truncating f to a neighbourhood of the orbit.

items.name: Endoscopic data and matching for the twisted Lie algebra Herm(W_1)
items.statement: An elliptic endoscopic datum for Herm(W_1) is one for U(W_1): (U(V_a) × U(V_b), s, ξ) with a + b = n, s ∈ Û(W_1) semisimple and ξ : Û(V_a) × Û(V_b) ↪ Û(W_1) onto the neutral component of the centralizer of s. Regular semisimple δ ∈ Herm(W), δ′ ∈ Herm(W′) are Jacquet–Langlands transfers if they are GL_n(E)-conjugate in gl_n(E) (after W ≅ E^n ≅ W′); then δ′ = Ad(g)δ and inv(δ, δ′) = [σ ↦ g^{-1}σ(g)] ∈ H^1(F, T_δ) extends the invariant on D(T_δ/F). δ and (δ_a, δ_b) match if δ and φ_{a,b}(δ_a, δ_b) are Jacquet–Langlands transfers, for φ_{a,b} : Herm(V_a) ⊕ Herm(V_b) ↪ Herm(W_{a,b}), W_{a,b} = V_a ⊕ V_b (Definition 2.6); a nice matching pair is one with φ_{a,b}(δ_a, δ_b) = δ.
items.note: ET.0 plans endoscopic triples, transport of stable classes under inner twists and matching of strongly regular classes; Herm(V) is the Lie algebra of U(V) up to the scalar ε, and the paper is an explicit source for the unitary Lie-algebra case.

items.name: κ-orbital and stable orbital integrals on Herm(W_1)
items.statement: For y ∈ Herm(W_1)^rss and f ∈ C_c^∞(Herm(W_1)), Orb(f, y) = ∫_{T_y\U(W_1)} f(g^{-1}yg) dg; over a nonarchimedean field the rational classes O_st(y) in the stable class form a D(T_y/F)-torsor, trivialized by inv(y, −) (2.5); for the character κ : D(T_y/F) → ℂ^× attached to an endoscopic datum, Orb^κ(f, y) = Σ_{y′∼_st y} κ(inv(y, y′)) Orb(f, y′), and SO = Orb^1.
items.note: ET.1 plans stable and κ-weighted sums of regular semisimple orbital integrals.

items.name: Lemma 2.7 (the endoscopic character κ on Herm)
items.statement: For matching y and (y_a, y_b), H^1(F, T_y) = ∏_{S_1} ℤ/2ℤ = ∏_{S_1(a)} ℤ/2ℤ × ∏_{S_1(b)} ℤ/2ℤ = H^1(F, T_{y_a} × T_{y_b}) (2.6). If κ̃ : H^1(F, T_y) → ℂ^× is trivial on each factor from S_1(a) and nontrivial on each factor from S_1(b), then κ = κ̃|_{D(T_y/F)}.
items.note: Stated without proof (standard, cf. [Rog90, Ch. 3]).

items.name: The transfer factor for Herm(W_1) in the unitary case
items.statement: Δ : [Herm(V_a) ⊕ Herm(V_b)]^rss × Herm(W_1)^rss → ℂ vanishes on non-matching pairs and satisfies Δ((δ_a, δ_b), δ) Orb^κ(δ, f) = Δ((δ_a, δ_b), δ′) Orb^κ(δ′, f) for δ′ stably conjugate to δ. Explicitly, with the relative discriminant D(δ) = ∏_{x_a, x_b}(x_a − x_b) over the eigenvalues of δ_a and δ_b (the quotient of Weyl discriminants in Δ_IV of [LS87], Remark 2.8): for a nice matching pair with W ≅ W_{a,b}, Δ((δ_a, δ_b), δ) = η_{E/F}(D(δ))|D(δ)|_F (2.7); in general Δ((δ_a, δ_b), δ) = κ(inv(δ, δ′)) η_{E/F}(D(δ))|D(δ)|_F with δ′ = φ_{a,b}(δ_a, δ_b).
items.note: The general Langlands–Shelstad–Kottwitz factor ([LS87], [Kot99]) is planned in ET.1; this simplified formula is cited from [Les22, Appendix A]. The paper writes the datum as (U(V_a) × U(V_b), s, η) on p. 19; ξ is meant (sourceIssues E2).

items.name: Endoscopic smooth transfer on Herm(W_1)
items.statement: f ∈ C_c^∞(Herm(W_1)) and f_{a,b} ∈ C_c^∞(Herm(V_a) ⊕ Herm(V_b)) are smooth transfers if SO(f_{a,b}, (y_a, y_b)) = Δ((y_a, y_b), y) Orb^κ(f, y) for all matching regular semisimple y, (y_a, y_b), and SO(f_{a,b}, (y_a, y_b)) = 0 when no y matches (y_a, y_b).
items.note: ET.1 defines matching test functions by their stable orbital-integral identities.

items.name: Theorem 2.9 (existence of endoscopic transfer for Herm)
items.statement: For any f ∈ C_c^∞(Herm(W_1)) there exists a smooth transfer f_{a,b} ∈ C_c^∞(Herm(V_a) ⊕ Herm(V_b)).
items.note: Cited: first by combining Laumon–Ngô [LN08] and Waldspurger [Wal06], [Wal97], which ET.3 plans; Xiao's alternative proof through Jacquet–Rallis transfer [Xia18] is outlined in §4.2–4.3 (items of the relative-endoscopy route).

items.name: Relative elliptic endoscopic data, endoscopic symmetric pairs and the relative transfer factor
items.statement: Over a nonarchimedean field (|𝒱_n| = 2), a relative elliptic endoscopic datum of 𝔲(W)_1 is Ξ = (U(V_a) × U(V_b), s, ξ, α, β) with (U(V_a) × U(V_b), s, ξ) an elliptic endoscopic datum of U(W_1) and α ∈ 𝒱_a, β ∈ 𝒱_b Hermitian forms, V_α = (E^a, α), V_β = (E^b, β). Its endoscopic symmetric pair is (U(V_a) × U(V_α), 𝔲(V_a ⊕ V_α)_1) ⊕ (U(V_b) × U(V_β), 𝔲(V_b ⊕ V_β)_1) with contraction r_{α,β}(δ_a, δ_b) = (r(δ_a), r(δ_b)). δ ∈ 𝔲(W)_1^rss matches (δ_a, δ_b) if r(δ) and r_{α,β}(δ_a, δ_b) match (§2.2.1), and Δ_rel((δ_a, δ_b), δ) := Δ(r_{α,β}(δ_a, δ_b), r(δ)).
items.note: Compatible with the general endoscopic symmetric varieties of [Les24] (Remark 1.2).

items.name: Relative κ-orbital and stable relative orbital integrals
items.statement: For δ ∈ 𝔲(W)_1^rss and Ξ, Lemma 2.3 transports κ to D(H_δ/F); RO^κ(f, δ) = Σ_{δ′∼_st δ} κ(inv(δ, δ′)) RO(f, δ′) over rational orbits in the stable orbit of δ, with inv(δ, δ′) := inv(r(δ), r(δ′)); SRO = RO^1.

items.name: Definition 2.10 (relative smooth transfer)
items.statement: f ∈ C_c^∞(𝔲(W)_1) and f_{α,β} ∈ C_c^∞(𝔲(V_a ⊕ V_α)_1 ⊕ 𝔲(V_b ⊕ V_β)_1) match if (1) SRO(f_{α,β}, (δ_a, δ_b)) = Δ_rel((δ_a, δ_b), δ) RO^κ(f, δ) for matching regular semisimple orbits (2.8), and (2) SRO(f_{α,β}, (δ_a, δ_b)) = 0 when no δ matches (δ_a, δ_b).
items.note: Existence of transfers is conjectured in [Les19, Conjecture 4.4]; Remark 2.11 asserts (without proof) independence of the choice r = r_1.

items.name: Theorem 2.12 = Theorem 1.3 (the relative endoscopic fundamental lemma)
items.statement: Let E/F be an unramified quadratic extension of nonarchimedean local fields of characteristic zero, V_n = W_1 = W_2 split with self-dual lattice Λ_n, so 𝔲(W)_1 = End(V_n) ⊃ End(Λ_n) compact open, and for an elliptic relative endoscopic datum Ξ fix V_n ≅ V_a ⊕ V_b with Λ_n = Λ_a ⊕ Λ_b self-dual. If (α, β) = (I_a, I_b), the functions 1_{End(Λ_n)} and 1_{End(Λ_a)} ⊗ 1_{End(Λ_b)} match; otherwise 1_{End(Λ_n)} matches 0.
items.note: Conjectured in [Les19], where n = 2, a = b = 1 was computed. The proof: Proposition 3.12 (Theorem 3.5 ⇒ 2.12), Propositions 4.8 and 5.2 (Theorem 5.3 ⇒ 3.5), and Theorem 5.3 from Theorem 11.1. Motivated by Conjecture 1.1 (a case of Getz–Wambach) on unitary Friedberg–Jacquet periods.

items.name: The Satake transform for GL_n(E)
items.statement: For E/F unramified, Sat(f)(s_1, …, s_n) = ∫_{GL_n(E)} f(g) ∏_i |a_i|_E^{s_i − (n+1−2i)/2} dg (g = nak Iwasawa, a = diag(a_i)) (3.1) is an algebra isomorphism ℋ_{K_{n,E}}(GL_n(E)) ≅ ℂ[q^{±2s_1}, …, q^{±2s_n}]^{S_n} ≅ ℂ[T̂_n]^{S_n} = ℂ[Z_1^{±1}, …, Z_n^{±1}]^{S_n}, with t_i = q^{−2s_i} = Z_i(t) (3.2).
items.note: SR.4 constructs the Satake isomorphism and verifies GL_n explicitly.

items.name: The Hecke algebra morphism ξ_(a,b)
items.statement: For n = a + b and the standard parabolic P_(a,b) = M_(a,b)N_(a,b) with M_(a,b) ≅ GL_a × GL_b, the dual embedding GL_a(ℂ) × GL_b(ℂ) → GL_n(ℂ), (m_1, m_2) ↦ diag(μ_b(ϖ)m_1, μ_a(ϖ)m_2) with μ_s(t) = |t|_E^{s/2}, corresponds to π_1 ⊠ π_2 ↦ Ind_{P_(a,b)(E)}^{GL_n(E)}(π_1(μ_b ∘ det) ⊠ π_2(μ_a ∘ det)) (normalized induction, not preserving temperedness) and induces ξ_(a,b) : ℋ_{K_{n,E}}(GL_n(E)) → ℋ_{K_{a,E}}(GL_a(E)) ⊗ ℋ_{K_{b,E}}(GL_b(E)) and ξ̂_(a,b) on the Satake side (3.3).
items.note: §1.3 describes it as related to a non-tempered version of parabolic induction.

items.name: Lemma 3.1 (ξ_(a,b) by parabolic descent)
items.note: Proof: 'a direct consequence of the Satake isomorphism' [Mínguez 2011].

items.name: Parabolic descent is dual to restriction to the Levi under Satake
items.statement: On spherical Hecke algebras, the parabolic descent f ↦ f^P to a Levi M corresponds under the Satake transforms of G and M to restriction along the dual embedding of M̂ in Ĝ; for GL_n and M = GL_a × GL_b, P_λ(Z_1, …, Z_n; q^{-2}) ↦ P_λ(X_1, …, X_a, Y_1, …, Y_b; q^{-2}).
items.note: Cited from Mínguez [M11, Proposition 4.6 (2)].

items.name: Macdonald's formula for spherical functions of GL_n(E)
items.statement: For a dominant coweight λ, Sat(1_{K_{n,E}ϖ^λK_{n,E}}) = q^{⟨λ, 2ρ⟩} P_λ(Z_1, …, Z_n; q^{-2}), where P_λ(x; t) = V(t) Σ_{σ∈S_n} σ(x^λ ∏_{λ_i>λ_j} (x_i − t x_j)/(x_i − x_j)) is the Hall–Littlewood polynomial and q is the residue cardinality of F.
items.note: Cited from Macdonald [Mac15, p. 299]; V(t) as in [Mac15, p. 208].

items.name: Hall–Littlewood polynomials: basis, homogeneity and branching
items.statement: As λ ranges over P^+_{n,d} = {λ ∈ ℤ^n_{≥0} dominant, Σλ_i = d} for all d ≥ 0, the P_λ(x_1, …, x_n; t) form a ℤ[t]-basis of ℤ[t][x_1, …, x_n]^{S_n}; P_λ is homogeneous of degree |λ|; and P_λ(X_i, Y_j; t) = Σ_{d_a+d_b=d} P_{d_a,d_b,λ} with P_{d_a,d_b,λ} = Σ_{α∈P^+_{a,d_a}, β∈P^+_{b,d_b}} c_{α,β}(λ) P_α(X; t)P_β(Y; t) its (d_a, d_b)-homogeneous part (3.6).
items.note: Cited from [Mac15], including III (5.5) for the coefficients.

items.name: Lemma 3.2 (ξ̂_(a,b) on Satake variables)
items.statement: ξ̂_(a,b) is the restriction to symmetric polynomials of ℂ[Z_1^{±1}, …, Z_n^{±1}] → ℂ[X^{±1}] ⊗ ℂ[Y^{±1}], Z_i ↦ q^{−b}X_i (i ≤ a), Z_i ↦ q^{−a}Y_{i−a} (i ≥ a+1).
items.note: Proof by Macdonald's formula, homogeneity of Hall–Littlewood polynomials and Lemma 3.1.

items.name: The Hermitian symmetric variety X_n and its endoscopic varieties
items.statement: X_n = (Res_{E/F}GL_n/U(V_n))(F) = {y ∈ Herm(V_n) : det y ≠ 0} = {x ∈ GL_n(E) : ᵗx̄ = x}, with twisted action g ∗ y = g y ᵗḡ of GL_n(E) and the U(V_n)-action; X_n ≅ ⊔_{x∈𝒱_n} GL_n(E)/U(V_x); X_n^rss = X_n ∩ Herm(V_n)^rss (the invariant-theoretic locus). For an elliptic endoscopic datum (U(V_a) × U(V_b), s, ξ) of Herm(V_n), every (y_a, y_b) matching y ∈ X_n^rss lies in X_a × X_b, which is the endoscopic symmetric variety of the Galois pair (GL_n(E), U(V_n)) (Remark 3.3); Ω = r(GL_n(E)) ⊂ X_n.

items.name: K_{n,E}-orbits on X_n (Jacobowitz)
items.statement: For E/F unramified, X_n = ⊔_{λ∈P_n} K_{n,E} ∗ ϖ^λ (3.7), where P_n = {λ ∈ ℤ^n : λ_1 ≥ … ≥ λ_n} and ϖ^λ = diag(ϖ^{λ_1}, …, ϖ^{λ_n}).
items.note: Cited from Jacobowitz [Jac62] (classification of Hermitian lattices over local fields); GN.2 plans integral and Hermitian lattice theory.

items.name: The spherical Hecke module ℋ_{K_{n,E}}(X_n)
items.statement: ℋ_{K_{n,E}}(X_n) = C_c^∞(X_n)^{K_{n,E}} with basis {1_λ}_{λ∈P_n}, 1_λ the indicator of K_{n,E} ∗ ϖ^λ and 1_0 = 1_{X_n(O_F)}; ℋ_{K_{n,E}}(GL_n(E)) acts by f ∗ φ(y) = ∫_{GL_n(E)} f(g^{-1}) φ(g ∗ y) dg. The distinguished rank-one submodule is − ∗ 1_0 : ℋ_{K_{n,E}}(GL_n(E)) ↪ ℋ_{K_{n,E}}(X_n), and − ∗ 1_0 also denotes f_a ⊗ f_b ↦ (f_a ∗ 1_0) ⊗ (f_b ∗ 1_0) into ℋ(X_a) ⊗ ℋ(X_b).

items.name: Proposition 3.4 (Hironaka: the Hecke module of X_n is free of rank 2^n)
items.statement: As an ℋ_{K_{n,E}}(GL_n(E))-module, ℋ_{K_{n,E}}(X_n) is free of rank 2^n.
items.note: Cited from Hironaka [Hir99, Theorem 2].

items.name: Hironaka's spherical Fourier transform and base change
items.statement: Hironaka's spherical Fourier transform gives an isomorphism of ℋ_{K_{n,E}}(GL_n(E))-modules H : ℋ_{K_{n,E}}(X_n) ≅ ℋ_{K_n}(GL_n(F)), where the module structure on the right is through the injective base change homomorphism BC : ℋ_{K_{n,E}}(GL_n(E)) → ℋ_{K_n}(GL_n(F)), with H(f ∗ 1_0) = BC(f); the algebra structure of ℋ_{K_{n,E}}(X_n) is transported from ℋ_{K_n}(GL_n(F)) via H.
items.note: Cited from [Hir99]; Remark 3.7 conjectures that ξ_(a,b) extends to all of ℋ_{K_{n,E}}(X_n) (with augmented transfer factors).

items.name: Theorem 3.5 = Proposition 1.5 (endoscopic fundamental lemma for the Hecke module of X_n)
items.statement: For E/F unramified and any φ ∈ ℋ_{K_{n,E}}(GL_n(E)), the functions φ ∗ 1_0 and ξ_(a,b)(φ) ∗ 1_0 (extended by zero to Herm(V_n) and Herm(V_a) ⊕ Herm(V_b)) are smooth transfers of each other in the sense of Theorem 2.9.
items.note: New explicit endoscopic transfers on the twisted Lie algebra generalizing the fundamental lemma of Laumon–Ngô [LN08]; the fundamental lemma for the Hecke algebra of the Galois pair (Res_{E/F}GL_n, U_n) (Remark 3.3; [Les24, §10]).

items.name: The contracted function Φ^n = r_!1_{End(Λ_n)} and the density m_0
items.statement: Φ^n := r_!1_{End(Λ_n)} on Ω_reg, extended by zero to X_n, is locally constant and almost compactly supported: with X_{n,d} = {h ∈ X_n : |det h|_F = q^{−d}}, Φ^n_d = Φ^n · 1_{X_{n,d}} ∈ C_c^∞(X_n). For T ∈ X_n, m_0(T) = ∫_{U(V_n)} 1_{End(Λ_n)}(xh) dh if T = xx^τ with x ∈ GL_n(E), and 0 otherwise (3.8); m_0(T) = #{[h] ∈ U(V_n)/U(Λ_n) : xh ∈ End(Λ_n)}.

items.name: m_0 is a local representation density
items.statement: For T = xx^τ and L = x^τΛ_n, m_0(T) = Den(L) = #{L ⊂ L′ ⊂ L^∨ : L′ self-dual}, and m_0(T) = 0 unless T is integral, i.e. L ⊂ Λ_n ⊂ L^∨ = x^{-1}Λ_n.
items.note: Uses [LZ22, (3.6.1.1)] (the lattice-counting formula for the normalized density) and U(V_n)-conjugacy of self-dual lattices; Remark 3.9 notes it is not used in the proof.

items.name: Lemma 3.8 (Φ^n in the spherical basis)
items.statement: Φ^n_d ≡ 0 if d is odd or d < 0, and Φ^n_{2d} = Σ_{λ∈P^+_{n,2d}} m_0(ϖ^λ) 1_λ.
items.note: Uses det(x) ∈ Nm(O_E) on the support, E/F unramified, and the orbit decomposition (3.7).

items.name: Corollary 3.10 (reformulation of Theorem 2.12)
items.statement: Theorem 2.12 holds if and only if, for every d ∈ ℤ_{≥0}, Φ^n_{2d} and Σ_{d_a+d_b=d} Φ^a_{2d_a} ⊗ Φ^b_{2d_b} match in the sense of Theorem 2.9.
items.note: From Lemma 2.5 and Lemma 3.8.

items.name: Lemma 3.11 (r_! on the Hecke algebra)
items.note: Uses vol(U(Λ_n)) = 1 and r_!(φ ∗ φ_1) = φ ∗ r_!(φ_1).

items.name: Proposition 3.12 (Theorem 3.5 implies Theorem 2.12)
items.note: §3 announces this as 'Proposition Prop: initial reduction' (a broken reference, sourceIssues E3). (3.10) from the Iwasawa decomposition and ∫_{N_n(E)} 1_d(uϖ^λ) du = q^{Σ(i−1)2λ_i} for λ ∈ ℤ^n_{d,+} [Off09, §6]; (3.9) from Lemma 3.2 and concatenation ℤ^a_{d_a,+} ⊕ ℤ^b_{d_b,+} → ℤ^n_{d,+}.

items.name: The Lie-algebra Jacquet–Rallis comparison and its matching of orbits
items.statement: Linear side gl_n(F) × F^n × F_n with diagonal GL_n(F)-action; invariants χ(x, v, v*) = (a, b), a_i the coefficients of det(tI − x), b_i = v*(x^i v); (x, v, v*) is regular semisimple iff det(⟨v*, x^{i+j}v⟩)_{i,j} ≠ 0, with trivial stabilizer, and regular semisimple elements with equal invariants are GL_n(F)-conjugate [RS07]. Unitary side Herm(V) × V with U(V), invariants a_i and b_i = ⟨w, y^i w⟩_V. Both quotients are 𝒜 ≅ 𝔸^{2n} [Cha19, Proposition 2.2.2.1]; each a ∈ 𝒜^rss(F) has one GL_n(F)-orbit and, in each Herm(V) × V, none or one U(V)-orbit, giving the bijection [GL_n(F)\gl_n(F) × F^n × F_n]^rss ≅ ⊔_{V∈𝒱_n} [U(V)\Herm(V) × V]^rss (4.2).
items.note: The unitary invariant is printed b_i = ⟨w, x^i w⟩_V on p. 32; y^i is meant (sourceIssues E4).

items.name: Jacquet–Rallis orbital integrals, transfer factor and transfer (4.3)
items.statement: Orb^{GL_n(F),η}(f, (x, v, v*)) = ∫_{GL_n(F)} f(Ad(g)x, gv, v*g^{-1}) η(det g) dg; Orb^{U(V)}(f, (y, w)) = ∫_{U(V)} f(Ad(g)y, gw) dg; transfer factor ω(x, v, v*) = η(det[v | xv | … | x^{n−1}v]) (4.1) [Zha14b, §3]; f and {f_V}_V are Jacquet–Rallis transfers if ω(x, v, v*) Orb^{GL_n(F),η}(f, (x, v, v*)) = Orb^{U(V)}(f_V, (y, w)) for all matching regular semisimple elements (4.3).

items.name: The gl_{n+1} variant of Jacquet–Rallis transfer (4.7)
items.statement: The embeddings gl_n(F) × F^n × F_n ↪ gl_{n+1}(F), (x, v, v*) ↦ (x, v; v*, 0), and Herm(V) × V ↪ Herm(V ⊕ Ee_0), (y, w) ↦ (y, w; ⟨w, −⟩_V, 0) with ⟨e_0, e_0⟩ = 1, give C_c^∞(gl_{n+1}(F)) ≅ C_c^∞(gl_n(F) × F^n × F_n) ⊗ C_c^∞(F) (4.4) and the unitary analogue (4.5). X = (x, v; v*, d) and Y = (y, w; ⟨w, −⟩, λ) match if (x, v, v*) and (y, w) match and d = λ; Orb^{GL_n(F),η}(f, X) = ∫_{GL_n(F)} f(Ad(g)X) η(det g) dg, Orb^{U(V)}(f_V, Y) = ∫_{U(V)} f_V(Ad(h)Y) dh, ω(X) = η(det[e_{n+1} | Xe_{n+1} | … | X^n e_{n+1}]) (4.6), and f, {f_V} are transfers if ω(X) Orb^{GL_n(F),η}(f, X) = Orb^{U(V)}(f_V, Y) (4.7).
items.note: The unitary embedding is printed with top-left entry x on p. 33; y is meant (sourceIssues E5). Remark 4.1 distinguishes the two notions.

items.name: Theorem 4.2 (Zhang: existence of Jacquet–Rallis transfer for the Lie algebra)
items.statement: For any f ∈ C_c^∞(gl_{n+1}(F)) there exists a transfer {f_V}_{V∈𝒱_n} in the sense of (4.7); conversely, any {f_V}_V has a transfer f.
items.note: Cited from W. Zhang [Zha14b]. Part 1 does not use it; Part 2 does.

items.name: Theorem 4.3 (the Jacquet–Rallis fundamental lemma for the Lie algebra)
items.statement: For E/F an unramified extension of p-adic fields and V = V_n split, 1_{gl_{n+1}(O_F)} and {1_{Herm(V_n ⊕ Ee_0)(O_F)}, 0} are Jacquet–Rallis transfers.
items.note: Cited: Yun [Yun11] in characteristic p > n + 1, transferred to characteristic zero for large residue characteristic by Gordon's appendix (printed 'Gordan', sourceIssues E6); Beuzart-Plessis [BP21b] in characteristic zero for all residue characteristics; global proofs by W. Zhang (p ≥ n) and Z. Zhang (p > 2).

items.name: Proposition 4.5 (Xiao: torsor structure on stable-and-Jacquet–Langlands classes)
items.statement: For δ ∈ Herm(V) regular semisimple, let S be the set of rational classes in the stable class of δ together with the classes in Herm(V′) (V′ the other Hermitian space) that are Jacquet–Langlands transfers of δ. There is a natural H^1(F, T_δ)-torsor structure on S extending the D(T_δ/F)-torsor structure on the stable class; in particular S ≅ ∏_{S_1} ℤ/2ℤ.
items.note: Cited from Xiao [Xia18, Proposition 3.8].

items.name: Generalized nilpotent orbital integrals
items.statement: For (x, v, v*) regular semisimple with F[x] = ∏F_i, T_x = F[x]^×, T_1 = ∏_{S_1}F_i^×, F^n = ⊕M_i (M_i = F_i·F^n), v = (v_i), v* = (v*_i) (all v_i, v*_i ≠ 0), and Σ ⊂ S_1 with v_Σ (resp. v*_{S_1∖Σ}) the vector keeping the components in Σ (resp. S_1 ∖ Σ): Orb^{GL_n(F),η}(f, (x, v_Σ, v*_{S_1∖Σ})) = ∫_{GL_n(F)/T_x} (∫_{T_1} f(Ad(g)x, gtv_Σ, v*_{S_1∖Σ}t^{-1}g^{-1}) ∏_{i∈Σ}|t_i|^s ∏_{i∈S_1∖Σ}|t_i|^{−s} η(det t)η(det g) dt)|_{s=0} dg, via meromorphic continuation; these are (GL_n(F), η)-invariant distributions supported on non-regular orbits in canonical bijection with the subsets of S_1.
items.note: After Xiao [Xia18].

items.name: Lemma 4.6 (Xiao: parametrizing S by norm classes)
items.statement: For ζ ∈ F[x]^× let (δ_ζ, w_ζ) ∈ Herm(V_ζ) × V_ζ represent the unique regular semisimple orbit matching (x, v, v*ζ), and (δ, w) = (δ_1, w_1). Then ζ ↦ δ_ζ is a bijection of H^1(F, T_δ)-torsors F[x]^×/Nm_{E[x]/F[x]}(E[x]^×) ≅ S ≅ H^1(F, T_δ); κ_Σ(δ_ζ) = (−1)^{Σ(ζ)}, Σ(ζ) = #{i ∉ Σ : ζ_i ∉ Nm(E_i)}, defines characters of H^1(F, T_δ), and every character arises for some Σ ⊂ S_1.
items.note: Cited from [Xia18, Lemma 4.6].

items.name: Theorem 4.7 (Xiao's germ expansion)
items.statement: If f and {f_V}_V are Jacquet–Rallis transfers (4.3), then for every regular semisimple (x, v, v*), ω(x, v, v*) Orb^{GL_n(F),η}(f, (x, v_Σ, v*_{S_1∖Σ})) = Σ_{ζ∈S} κ_Σ(ζ) ∫_{U(V_ζ)/T_{δ_ζ}} f_{V_ζ}(Ad(g)δ_ζ, 0) dg.
items.note: Cited from [Xia18, Theorem 4.7]; the right side is a κ-orbital integral of f_V(−, 0) after Jacquet–Langlands transfer of f_{V′}.

items.name: Xiao's construction of endoscopic transfer through Jacquet–Rallis transfer
items.statement: For P_(a,b) ⊂ GL_n(F) with Lie algebra 𝔭_(a,b), the Lie-algebraic parabolic descent of φ ∈ C_c^∞(gl_n(F) × F^n × F_n) is φ_𝔭((m_1, m_2), v, v*) = ∫_{𝔫_(a,b)} ∫_{K_n} φ(k(m_1, n; 0, m_2)k^{-1}, kv, v*k^{-1}) dk dn (Definition 4.9). Given f ∈ C_c^∞(Herm(V_n)), choose F with ev_0(F) = F(−, 0) = f, a Jacquet–Rallis transfer φ of {F, 0}, Jacquet–Rallis transfers F^{a,b}_{α,β} ∈ C_c^∞(Herm(V_α) × V_α × Herm(V_β) × V_β) of φ_𝔭, f^{a,b}_{α,β} = ev_0(F^{a,b}_{α,β}), their Jacquet–Langlands transfers f̃^{a,b}_{α,β} to Herm(V_a) ⊕ Herm(V_b), and f^{a,b} = Σ_{α,β}(−1)^{k(α,β)} f̃^{a,b}_{α,β}, k(α, β) the number of split forms among α, β. Then f^{a,b} is an endoscopic transfer of f.
items.note: The last assertion is cited from [Xia18, Theorem 6.1]; this reproves Theorem 2.9.

items.name: Proposition 4.8 (second reduction)
items.statement: With Λ_n = O_E^n, L_n = O_F^n × O_{F,n} and the embeddings ℋ(X_n) ↪ C_c^∞(Herm(V_n) × V_n), f ↦ f ⊗ 1_{Λ_n}, and ℋ_{K_n}(GL_n(F)) ↪ C_c^∞(gl_n(F) × F^n × F_n) via 1_{L_n}: if for every φ ∈ ℋ_{K_{n,E}}(GL_n(E)) the functions {(φ ∗ 1_0) ⊗ 1_{Λ_n}, 0} and BC(φ) ⊗ 1_{L_n} are Jacquet–Rallis transfers (4.3), then Theorem 3.5 holds.
items.note: Proof: Xiao's construction and Theorem 4.7, with BC(ξ_(a,b)(φ)) = ξ′_(a,b)(BC(φ)) (μ′_s(t) = |t|_F^{s/2}) and ξ′_(a,b)(φ) ⊗ 1_{L_a×L_b} = (φ ⊗ 1_{L_n})_𝔭. The proof prints 'F = φ ⊗ 1_{Λ_n} so that ev_0(F) = φ'; (φ ∗ 1_0) ⊗ 1_{Λ_n} is meant (sourceIssues E7).

items.name: Weil representations on Jacquet–Rallis test functions and orbital integrals
items.statement: For ψ of conductor O_F, q(x, v, v*) = v*(v) and q(y, w) = ⟨w, w⟩_V, the partial Fourier transforms F(f)(x, v, v*) = ∫_{F^n×F_n} f(x, w, w*) ψ(w*(v) + v*(w)) dw dw* and F(f)(y, w) = ∫_V f(y, u) ψ(Tr_{E/F}⟨u, w⟩) du, together with W(1, t; 0, 1)φ = ψ(t q)φ and W(0, 1; −1, 0)φ = Fφ, define Weil representations of SL_2(F) on C_c^∞(gl_n(F) × F^n × F_n) and C_c^∞(Herm(V) × V). On the spaces Orb(gl_n(F) × F^n × F_n) and Orb(Herm(V) × V) of functions a ↦ O(a, f) on 𝒜^rss(F) (O(a, f′) = ω(X_a)Orb^{GL_n(F),η}(f′, X_a); O(a, f) = Orb^{U(V)}(f, Y_a) or 0), set W(1, t; 0, 1)Φ(a) = ψ(t q(a))Φ(a) and W(0, 1; −1, 0)O(a, f) = O(a, F(f)); f′ and f are transfers (4.3) iff O(a, f′) = O(a, f).
items.note: MetaplecticAutomorphicForms MP.2 plans the general Weil representation. The unitary Fourier transform is printed ∫_V f(x, u) ψ(Nm_{E/F}(⟨u, w⟩)) du on p. 40; the trace pairing is meant (sourceIssues E8).

items.name: Proposition 5.1 (Beuzart-Plessis: the Weil representations descend to orbital integrals)
items.statement: The Weil representations on C_c^∞(gl_n(F) × F^n × F_n) and C_c^∞(Herm(V) × V) descend to Weil representations on Orb(gl_n(F) × F^n × F_n) and Orb(Herm(V) × V), and these coincide on the intersection.
items.note: Cited from [BP21b, Proposition 1], resting on the compatibility of Jacquet–Rallis transfer with Fourier transform [Zha14b, Theorem 4.17].

items.name: Proposition 5.2 (third reduction)
items.statement: If for φ ∈ ℋ_{K_{n,E}}(GL_n(E)) the functions {φ ∗ 1_0, 0} and BC(φ) are Jacquet–Rallis transfers in the sense of (4.7) (for gl_n rather than gl_{n+1}), then {(φ ∗ 1_0) ⊗ 1_{Λ_n}, 0} and BC(φ) ⊗ 1_{L_n} are transfers in the sense of (4.3).
items.note: Proof as in [BP21b]: Φ_φ(a) vanishes for |q(a)| > 1 and, by the hypothesis, for |q(a)| = 1 (5.1); it is F-invariant and invariant under N(𝔭^{-1}), hence under SL_2(F), so Φ_φ = 0 where q(a) ≠ 0.

items.name: Proposition 1.6 (a Jacquet–Rallis fundamental lemma for the Hecke module)
items.statement: Let E/F be unramified, Λ_n ⊂ V_n self-dual, L_n = O_F^n × O_{F,n} and BC : ℋ_{K_{n,E}}(GL_n(E)) → ℋ_{K_n}(GL_n(F)) the base change homomorphism. For any φ ∈ ℋ_{K_{n,E}}(GL_n(E)), {(φ ∗ 1_0) ⊗ 1_{Λ_n}, 0} and BC(φ) ⊗ 1_{L_n} are smooth transfers for the Jacquet–Rallis transfer (4.3).
items.note: Generalizes Yun's Jacquet–Rallis fundamental lemma [Yun11]. Proved by Proposition 5.2 and Theorem 5.3; it gives Theorem 3.5 by Proposition 4.8.

items.name: Theorem 5.3 = Theorem 1.7 (final reduction: Jacquet–Rallis transfer of the Hecke module)
items.statement: For E/F unramified, any φ ∈ ℋ_{K_{n,E}}(GL_n(E)) and any X ∈ GL_n(F)^rss, ω(X) Orb^{GL_{n−1}(F),η}(BC(φ), X) = Orb^{U(V_{n−1})}(φ ∗ 1_0, Y) if X matches Y ∈ X_n^rss, and 0 otherwise.
items.note: Proved in §11.2 from Theorem 11.1 with n − 1 in place of n: Φ = 1_{K_{n−1,E}} ⊗ φ lifts φ under (7.5), BC(Φ)~ = BC(φ) = H(φ ∗ 1_0) by Hironaka's commutative diagram, and the reductions (7.6), (7.7) identify the orbital integrals; the split form w_n may be replaced by I_n as E/F is unramified. Propositions 4.8 and 5.2 with Theorem 5.3 give Theorem 3.5.

items.name: The twisted Jacquet–Rallis set-up
items.statement: w_n = antidiag(1, −1, …, (−1)^{n−1}), g^θ = w_n ᵗg^{-1} w_n, g^σ = ḡ; V_n = V_{w_n} (n odd) or V_{ξw_n} (n even, ξ trace zero), so U(V_n) = Res_{E/F}GL_n^{θ∘σ} is quasi-split and V_n is split globally and locally. G = GL_n × GL_{n+1} ⊃ H = GL_n embedded by g ↦ (g, diag(g, 1)); G′ = Res_{E/F}(GL_n × GL_{n+1}) ⊃ H′ = Res_{E/F}GL_n diagonally, and H′_{x,y} = U(V_x) × U(V_y) for (x, y) ∈ X_n × X_{n+1}; y(x) = diag(x, 1), V_{y(x)} = V_x ⊕ Ee_0 with ⟨e_0, e_0⟩ = 1. The matching compares H(F)\G(F)/H(F) with ⊔_{x,y} H′(F)\G′(F)/H′_{x,y}(F), switching the roles of the rational linear group and the unitary group in the Jacquet–Rallis comparison.

items.name: Generic representations, Whittaker models and the involution θ
items.statement: GR_n(F) is the set of generic representations of GL_n(F); ψ_0(u) = ψ(Σu_{i,i+1}), ψ′ = ψ ∘ Tr_{E/F}; GR^σ_n(E) the Galois-invariant generic representations of GL_n(E), each of the form Π = BC(π); W(π) = W^ψ(π) with right translation, and Ŵ(g) = W(g^θ) gives W(π)^θ ≅ W^{ψ^{-1}}(π^∨).

items.name: Local base change of Galois-invariant generic representations
items.statement: Every generic representation of GL_n(E) isomorphic to its Galois twist is the base change BC(π) of a generic representation π of GL_n(F).
items.note: Cited from Arthur–Clozel [AC89]; ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.5 registers cyclic base change with exact hypotheses.

items.name: Lemmas 7.1–7.2 (reduction of double cosets to a single orbit problem)
items.statement: (1) (h, g) ↦ h^{-1}g induces H(F)\G(F)^rss/H(F) ≅ GL_{n+1}(F)^rss/GL_n(F) (adjoint action). (2) For x ∈ X_n, with X^rss_{y(x)} the elements whose adjoint U(V_x)-orbit is closed of maximal dimension, (g_1, g_2) ↦ (g_1^{-1}g_2) y ᵗ(ḡ_1^{-1}ḡ_2) y(x) induces ⊔_{y∈𝒱_{n+1}} H′(F)\G′(F)^rss/H′_{x,y}(F) ≅ X^rss_{y(x)}/U(V_x).

items.name: Proposition 7.3 (matching of regular semisimple double cosets)
items.statement: There is a natural bijection H(F)\G(F)^rss/H(F) ≅ ⊔_{x∈𝒱_n} ⊔_{y∈𝒱_{n+1}} H′(F)\G′(F)^rss/H′_{x,y}(F); γ and δ match with respect to (x, y), γ ↔^{x,y} δ, if their orbits correspond.
items.note: Reduced to the Lie-algebra Jacquet–Rallis matching restricted to invertible elements: regular semisimple elements of gl_{n+1}(F) and Herm(V_{y(x)}) match iff they are GL_n(E)-conjugate in gl_{n+1}(E).

items.name: Invariant polynomials of the twisted comparison
items.statement: For X = (A, b; c, d) ∈ gl_{n+1}(F), c(X) = (a_1, …, a_n, b_0, …, b_{n−1}, d) with a_i = Tr(∧^iA), b_j = cA^jb (7.3)–(7.4); two regular semisimple elements of gl_{n+1}(F) and Herm(V_{y(x)}) match iff they have the same invariants [RS07]. On G(F), c_i(γ) = c_i(γ_1^{-1}γ_2); on G′(F), c^{x,y}_i(δ) = c_i(π_{x,y}(δ)) with π_{x,y}(δ) = (δ_1^{-1}δ_2) y ᵗ(δ̄_1^{-1}δ̄_2) y(x) ∈ X^y_{y(x)}.

items.name: Relative orbital integrals of the twisted comparison and the transfer factor Ω
items.statement: For f ∈ C_c^∞(G(F)), γ ∈ G(F)^rss: Orb^η(f, γ) = ∫_{H(F)}∫_{H(F)} f(h_1^{-1}γh_2) η(det h_2) dh_1 dh_2 = Orb^{GL_n(F),η}(f̃, γ_1^{-1}γ_2) (7.6) with f̃(g) = ∫_{H(F)} f(h^{-1}(1, g)) dh (7.5), f ↦ f̃ surjective onto C_c^∞(GL_{n+1}(F)). For f′ ∈ C_c^∞(G′(F)), δ ∈ G′(F)^rss: Orb(f′, δ) = ∫_{H′(F)}∫_{H′_{x,y}(F)} f′(h_1^{-1}δh_2) dh_1 dh_2 = Orb^{U(V_x)}(f̃′, π_{x,y}(δ)) (7.7) with f̃′(g y ᵗḡ y(x)) = ∫_{H′(F)}∫_{U(V_y)} f′(h^{-1}(1, gu)) dh du. The transfer factor is Ω(γ_1, γ_2) = ω(γ_1^{-1}γ_2) with ω as in (4.6) (Definition 7.4).

items.name: Z-regular semisimple elements
items.statement: Z_{G′}(F) × U(V_x) acts on X_{y(x)} by conjugation and (z_1, z_2) ∘ s = (z_1^{-1}z_2) s (z̄_1^{-1}z̄_2) (7.8); Z_0 = {[(z_1, z_2), z_1] : z_1 ∈ Z_{U(V_x)}(F), z_2 ∈ Z_{U(V_y)}(F)} ≅ Z_{U(V_x)}(F) × Z_{U(V_y)}(F) (7.9) acts trivially. s = (A, b; ⟨b, −⟩_x, d) is Z-regular semisimple if it is regular semisimple and Tr(A), d ∈ F^× (a Zariski-open dense set); δ is Z-regular semisimple if π_{x,y}(δ) is. On the linear side Z_G(F) × GL_n(F) acts on GL_{n+1}(F) by (z_1, z_2) ∘ g = diag(z_1^{-1}, 1) g z_2 (7.11), and g = (A, b; c, d) is Z-regular semisimple if regular semisimple with Tr(A), d ≠ 0; γ is if γ_1^{-1}γ_2 is.

items.name: Lemma 7.5 (stabilizers and closed orbits of Z-regular semisimple elements)
items.statement: A Z-regular semisimple s ∈ X_{y(x)} has stabilizer Z_0 under Z_{G′}(F) × U(V_x) and closed orbit, hence is Z_{G′} × U(V_x)-regular semisimple; two such elements lie in one orbit iff they agree under the invariants Tr(∧^iA)/Tr(A)^i and ⟨b, A^jb⟩_x/(Tr(A)^{j+1}d) (7.10) and Tr(A_1) ≡ Tr(A_2), d_1 ≡ d_2 mod Nm(E^×). The linear analogue holds with trivial stabilizer in Z_G(F) × GL_n(F).
items.note: Closedness as in [Zha14b, Lemma 2.1].

items.name: Remark 7.6 and Lemma 7.7 (the norm map on centers and Z-regular matching)
items.statement: The matching of Proposition 7.3 restricts to Z-regular semisimple loci, but for E/F a field gives only a surjection ⊔_{x,y} H′(F)\G′(F)^{Z−rss}/H′_{x,y}(F)Z_{G′}(F) → H(F)\G(F)^{Z−rss}/H(F)Z_G(F), 2-to-1 for F local; and if δ ↔ γ are Z-regular semisimple and z ∈ Z_{G′}(F), then δz matches γNm(z).
items.note: The remedy is to scale only by Nm(Z_{G′}(F)) ⊂ Z_G(F).

items.name: Orbital integrals with central character
items.statement: For F local, δ Z-regular semisimple and ω′ = ω ∘ Nm trivial on Z_{H′_{x,y}}(F): Orb_{ω′}(f′, δ) = ∫_{H′(F)}∫_{Z_{H′_{x,y}}(F)\H′_{x,y}(F)}∫_{Z_{G′}(F)} f′(h_1^{-1}δzh_2) ω′(z) dz dh_1 dh_2 = ∫_{Z_{G′}(F)} Orb(f′, zδ) ω(Nm z) dz (7.12), independent of the four choices of ω; for f ∈ C_c^∞(G(F)), Orb^η_ω(f, γ) = ∫_{Nm(Z_{G′}(F))} Orb^η(f, zγ) ω(z) dz (7.13), with Nm(Z_{G′}(F)) ≅ Nm_{E/F}(E^×)² of index 4 in Z_G(F). Both integrals converge absolutely.

items.name: Smooth transfer for the twisted comparison
items.statement: f ∈ C_c^∞(G(F)) and {f′_{x,y}}_{(x,y)∈𝒱_n×𝒱_{n+1}} ⊂ C_c^∞(G′(F)) match (are transfers) if Ω(γ) Orb^η(f, γ) = Orb(f′_{x,y}, δ) whenever γ ↔^{x,y} δ are regular semisimple (7.14).

items.name: Proposition 7.8 (explicit transfer in the split case)
items.statement: For E = F × F (𝒱_n, 𝒱_{n+1} singletons, η trivial), with U(V_x) ≅ {(g, g^θ) : g ∈ GL_n(F)} and U(V_y) ≅ {(g, g^θ) : g ∈ GL_{n+1}(F)}, the functions f_1 ⊗ f_2 ∈ C_c^∞(G(F) × G(F)) and f_1 ∗ f_2^{θ∨} ∈ C_c^∞(G(F)), f^{θ∨}(g) = f(g^{−θ}), are smooth transfers.
items.note: The paper omits the proof ('a simple computation'). U(V_y) is printed with g ∈ GL_n(F) on p. 54; GL_{n+1}(F) is meant (sourceIssues E9).

items.name: Theorem 7.9 (existence of smooth transfer for the twisted comparison)
items.statement: For E/F a quadratic extension of nonarchimedean fields, every f ∈ C_c^∞(G(F)) has a transfer {f′_{x,y}}_{x,y}, and every collection {f′_{x,y}} has a transfer f.
items.note: From Theorem 4.2 through (7.6) and (7.7).

items.name: Corollary 7.10 (transfer with central characters)
items.statement: If f and {f′_{x,y}} are transfers (E/F nonarchimedean), ω is a central character of G(F) and ω′ = ω ∘ Nm, then Ω(γ) Orb^η_ω(f, γ) = Orb_{ω′}(f′_{x,y}, δ) for matching Z-regular semisimple γ ↔^{x,y} δ (7.15).
items.note: Uses Lemma 7.7 and Ω(γNm(z)) = Ω(γ).

items.name: Lemma 7.11 (transfer supported on G[x, y])
items.statement: Let G[x, y] = {(g_1, g_2) : η(det g_1) = η(det x), η(det g_2) = η(det y)}. If E/F is split or F is nonarchimedean, for any f′_{x,y} ∈ C_c^∞(G′(F)) one may choose f ∈ C_c^∞(G(F)) with Ω(γ) Orb^η(f, γ) = Orb(f′_{x,y}, δ) for γ ↔^{x,y} δ and 0 otherwise (7.16), and supp(f) ⊂ G[x, y].
items.note: The map p(g_1, g_2) = g_1^{-1}g_2 restricted to each G[x_i, y_j] is a submersion onto G_{i+j} (7.17).

items.name: Theorem 7.12 (fundamental lemma for the unit element)
items.statement: For E/F an unramified quadratic extension of nonarchimedean local fields, K = G(O_F) and K′ = G′(O_F), 1_K and {f′_{x,y}} with f′_{x,y} = 1_{K′} for (x, y) = (w_n, w_{n+1}) and 0 otherwise are transfers.
items.note: From Theorem 4.3 restricted to |det X|_F = 1; with [BP21b] no residue-characteristic hypothesis is needed.

items.name: Petersson inner products and the canonical local Whittaker pairing
items.statement: For π cuspidal on GL_n(𝔸_F), π̂ ≅ π^∨ realized by φ^θ; (φ, φ̂) = ∫_{A_n GL_n(F)\GL_n(𝔸_F)} φφ̂ and ⟨φ, φ̂⟩_Pet = ∫_{Z(𝔸)GL_n(F)\GL_n(𝔸)} φφ̂; W_φ(g) = ∫_{[N_n]} φ(ng)ψ_0^{-1}(n) dn. The local pairing [W_v, Ŵ′_v]_{π_v} = I_0(W_v, Ŵ′_v), where I_s(W_v, Ŵ′_v) = L(n, 1_{F_v^×}) ∫_{N_n(F_v)\P_n(F_v)} W_v(h)Ŵ′_v(h)|det h|^s dh over the mirabolic P_n, is holomorphic at s = 0 and a nondegenerate GL_n(F_v)-invariant pairing [FLO12, Appendix A]; for unramified π_v and the normalized spherical W_v, [W_v, Ŵ_v]_{π_v} = L(1, π_v × π_v^∨).

items.name: Proposition 8.1 (factorization of the Petersson norm)
items.statement: For φ ∈ π factorizable, (φ, φ̂) = Res_{s=1}L(s, π × π^∨) ∏_v [W_v, Ŵ_v]^♮_{π_v} with [W_v, Ŵ_v]^♮ = [W_v, Ŵ_v]/L(1, π_v × π_v^∨) (8.1), equal to 1 for the normalized spherical vector; hence ⟨φ, φ̂⟩_Pet = Res_{s=1}L(s, π × π^∨)/vol(F^×\𝔸^1_F) ∏_v [W_v, Ŵ_v]^♮ (8.2), and similarly for Res_{E/F}GL_n.
items.note: Cited from [FLO12, §10.3].

items.name: Proposition 8.3 and Corollary 8.4 (factorization of Rankin–Selberg periods)
items.statement: For Π = Π_n ⊠ Π_{n+1} generic cuspidal on G(𝔸_F), λ_Π(φ) = ∫_{[GL_n]} φ_n(h)φ_{n+1}(diag(h, 1)) dh; the local λ_{Π_v}(s, W_v) = ∫_{N_n(F_v)\GL_n(F_v)} W_v(h)|det h|^s dh converges for Re s ≫ 0 (for Re s > −1/2 if Π_v is tempered, Remark 8.2) and λ^♮ = λ/L(s + 1/2, Π_v) is entire, λ^♮_{Π_v}(W_v) = λ^♮(0, W_v) spans the one-dimensional Hom_{H(F_v)}(Π_v, ℂ), and λ^♮ = 1 on the normalized spherical vector (8.3). For Π unitary and φ factorizable, λ_Π(φ) = L(1/2, Π_n × Π_{n+1}) ∏_v λ^♮_{Π_v}(W_v) (8.4), and for the twist λ^η_{Π_n⊠Π_{n+1}} = λ_{Π_n·η⊠Π_{n+1}}, λ^η_Π(φ) = L(1/2, Π_n × Π_{n+1} · η) ∏_v λ^{η_v,♮}_{Π_v}(W_v) (8.5).
items.note: Cited from Jacquet–Piatetski-Shapiro–Shalika [JPSS83]; AL.3 plans the Rankin–Selberg local integrals, unramified calculation and global unfolding.

items.name: Unitary periods, FLO spaces and (twisted) Bessel characters
items.statement: For Π cuspidal on GL_n(𝔸_E) and x ∈ X_n, P_x(φ) = ∫_{[U(V_x)]} φ(h) dh; Π is distinguished by U(V_x) if P_x ≢ 0. Locally, for Π_v tempered, E(X_n, W^{ψ′_v}(Π_v)^*) is the space of continuous GL_n(E_v)-invariant α : X_n(F_v) × W(Π_v) → ℂ, ≅ ⊕_{x∈𝒱_n} Hom_{U(V_x)}(W(Π_v), ℂ); the twisted Bessel character is J^α_{Π_v}(f′) = ⟨f′ · α, λ^∨_1⟩ with f′ · α : W ↦ ∫_{X_n(F_v)} f′(x)α(x, W) dx (identified with an element of W^{ψ′^{-1}}(Π^∨_v) via [·,·]) and λ^∨_1(Ŵ) = Ŵ(1); the Bessel character of π_v is I_{π_v}(f) = ⟨f · λ_{w_n}, λ^∨_1⟩ with f · λ_{w_n} : W ↦ ∫_{GL_n(F_v)} f(g)W(w_ng) dg.

items.name: Distinction of base changes by unitary groups (Jacquet; Feigon–Lapid–Offen)
items.statement: If Π = BC(π) for a cuspidal π of GL_n(𝔸_F), then Π is distinguished by the quasi-split U(V_n) [Jac10]; [FLO12, Corollary 10.3] generalizes this to other Hermitian forms.
items.note: Cited.

items.name: Jacquet's theorem: H′_{x,y}-distinguished representations are base changes
items.statement: If a cuspidal Π = Π_n ⊠ Π_{n+1} of G′(𝔸_F) is H′_{x,y}-distinguished, there is a cuspidal π = π_n ⊠ π_{n+1} of G(𝔸_F) with Π_i = BC(π_i); then π_i ≇ π_i · η, L(s, π × π^∨ · η) is holomorphic at s = 1, L(s, Π_i × Π^∨_i) = L(s, π_i × π^∨_i)L(s, π_i × π^∨_i · η) (8.11), and Res_{s=1}L(s, Π_i × Π^∨_i)/L(1, π_i × π^∨_i · η) = Res_{s=1}L(s, π_i × π^∨_i) ≠ 0 (8.12).
items.note: The base-change statement is cited from Jacquet [Jac05].

items.name: Theorem 8.5 (Feigon–Lapid–Offen functionals)
items.statement: For every π_v ∈ Temp(GL_n(F_v)) there is a unique α^{π_v} ∈ E(X_n, W^{ψ′_v}(BC(π_v))^*) with J^{α^{π_v}}_{BC(π_v)}(f′) = I_{π_v}(f) for all pairs (f, f′) of transfers in the sense of [FLO12, §3]. For E_v ≅ F_v × F_v, α^{π_v}_{(h, ᵗh)}(W′ ⊗ W″) = [W(h, π_v)W′, W(w_n, π̂_v)Ŵ″]_{π_v} (8.6).
items.note: Cited from [FLO12] (the split formula from [FLO12, Corollary 7.2]).

items.name: Lemma 8.6 (unramified value of the FLO functional)
items.statement: For F_v nonarchimedean of odd residue characteristic, E_v/F_v unramified, ψ′_v of conductor O_{F_v}, Π_v = BC(π_v) unramified with normalized spherical W_0, and x ∈ X_n(O_{F_v}) = GL_n(O_{E_v}) ∗ w_n: α^{π_v}_x(W_0) = L(1, π_v × π^∨_v · η_v). The normalized functional is α^{π_v,♮}_x = α^{π_v}_x/L(1, π_v × π^∨_v · η_v) (8.7).
items.note: Cited from [FLO12, Lemma 3.9].

items.name: Proposition 8.7 (factorization of unitary periods)
items.statement: For π cuspidal on GL_n(𝔸_F), Π = BC(π) and any x ∈ X_n, P_x(φ) = 2 L(1, π × π^∨ · η) ∏_v α^{π_v,♮}_x(W_v) (8.8), where W_Π(g : φ) = ∏_v W_v(g_v).
items.note: Cited from [FLO12, Theorem 10.2].

items.name: Global relative characters I_π and J^{x,y}_Π
items.statement: For π = π_n ⊠ π_{n+1} cuspidal on G(𝔸_F), I_π(f) = Σ_φ λ_π(π(f)φ) λ^η_{π^∨}(φ̂)/⟨φ, φ̂⟩_Pet over an orthogonal basis, φ̂(g) = φ(g^θ) (8.9). For Π cuspidal on G′(𝔸_F) and (x, y) ∈ 𝒱_n × 𝒱_{n+1}, with P_{x,y} = P_x ⊗ P_y, J^{x,y}_Π(f′) = Σ_φ λ_Π(Π(f′)φ) P_{x,y}(φ̂)/⟨φ, φ̂⟩_Pet (8.10); J^{x,y}_Π ≡ 0 unless Π is H′_{x,y}-distinguished.

items.name: Normalized local relative characters
items.statement: With W(Π_v) = W^{ψ′^{-1}_v}(Π_{n,v}) ⊗ W^{ψ′_v}(Π_{n+1,v}) and α^{π_v}_{x,y} = α^{π_{n,v},♮}_x ⊗ α^{π_{n+1,v},♮}_y: J^{x,y,♮}_{Π_v}(f′_v) = Σ_{W_v} λ^♮_{Π_v}(Π_v(f′_v)W_v) α^{π̂_v}_{x,y}(Ŵ_v)/[W, Ŵ]^♮_{Π_v} and I^♮_{π_v}(f_v) = Σ_{W_v} λ^♮_{π_v}(π_v(f_v)W_v) λ^{η_v,♮}_{π̂_v}(Ŵ_v)/[W, Ŵ]^♮_{π_v} over orthogonal bases; J^{x,y}_{Π_v}, I_{π_v} use unnormalized periods. J^{x,y,♮}_{Π_v} depends on an auxiliary π_v with Π_v = BC(π_v), but the global products do not (Remark 8.12).

items.name: Proposition 8.11 (factorization of J^{x,y}_Π)
items.statement: If J^{x,y}_Π ≢ 0 and Π = BC(π), then for factorizable f′, J^{x,y}_Π(f′) = 4 vol(E^×\𝔸^1_E)² L(1/2, Π_n × Π_{n+1})/Res_{s=1}L(s, π × π^∨) ∏_v J^{x,y,♮}_{Π_v}(f′_v) (8.13). Hence J^{x,y}_Π ≢ 0 iff L(1/2, Π_n × Π_{n+1}) ≠ 0 and every local α^{π_v}_{x,y} is nonzero.
items.note: From (8.2), (8.4), (8.8), (8.12) and the nonvanishing of local Rankin–Selberg periods [JPSS83].

items.name: Proposition 8.13 (factorization of I_π)
items.statement: For π cuspidal and factorizable f, I_π(f) = vol(F^×\𝔸^1_F)² L(1/2, Π_n × Π_{n+1})/Res_{s=1}L(s, π × π^∨) ∏_v I^♮_{π_v}(f_v) (8.14), Π_n ⊠ Π_{n+1} = BC(π_n) ⊠ BC(π_{n+1}); so I_π ≢ 0 iff L(1/2, Π_n × Π_{n+1}) ≠ 0.

items.name: Kernels, relative trace distributions and nice test functions
items.statement: K_f(x, y) = Σ_{γ∈G(F)} f(x^{-1}γy), I(f) = ∫_{[H]}∫_{[H]} K_f(h_1, h_2)η(det h_2); K_{f,ω} and I_ω with a central character; on the twisted side J^{x,y}(f′) = ∫_{[H′]}∫_{[H′_{x,y}]} K_{f′}(h_1, h_2) and J^{x,y}_{ω′} with ω′ = ω ∘ Nm trivial on (Z_{G′} ∩ H′_{x,y})(𝔸). f = ⊗f_v is ω-nice (Definition 9.1) if f_{v_1} is essentially a supercuspidal matrix coefficient w.r.t. ω_{v_1} at some finite place v_1 split in E, and f_{v_2} is supported in the Z-regular locus at another split place v_2 (possibly archimedean); likewise ω′-nice.
items.note: Remark 9.2 compares with Beuzart-Plessis's more flexible cuspidal Bernstein-component condition [BP21a].

items.name: Lemma 9.3 (convergence for nice test functions)
items.statement: For ω unitary and f ω-nice, K_f is compactly supported modulo H(F) × H(F) and K_{f,ω} modulo H(F) × H(F)Z_G(𝔸_F) on H(𝔸) × H(𝔸), so I(f) and I_ω(f) converge absolutely; I(f) = Σ_γ Orb^η(f, γ) over regular semisimple γ ∈ H(F)\G(F)/H(F), a finite sum of factorizable global orbital integrals.
items.note: Verbatim as [Zha14b, Lemma 2.2].

items.name: Lemma 9.4 (geometric side with the norm subgroup)
items.statement: With η_{i,j}(z_1, z_2) = η(z_1)^iη(z_2)^j and ω_{i,j} = ωη_{i,j}, for ω-nice f: (1/4) Σ_{(i,j)∈{0,1}²} I_{ω_{i,j}}(f) = Σ_γ Orb^η_ω(f, γ) over Z-regular semisimple γ ∈ H(F)\G(F)/Nm(Z_{G′}(F))H(F), with Orb^η_ω(f, γ) = ∫∫∫_{Nm(Z_{G′}(𝔸_F))} f(h_1^{-1}γzh_2)η(det h_2)ω(z) = ∏_v Orb^{η_v}_{ω_v}(f_v, γ_v).
items.note: Uses [Z_G(𝔸_F) : Z_G(F)Nm(Z_{G′}(𝔸_F))] = 4 and the Hasse norm theorem. The character is printed η(z)^iη(z)^j and the proof keeps a spurious Σ_{(i,j)} in its last line (sourceIssues E10, E11).

items.name: Hasse norm theorem for quadratic extensions
items.statement: For a quadratic extension E/F of number fields, an element of F^× is a norm from E^× iff it is a local norm everywhere; hence Z_G(F)\Z_G(F)Nm(Z_{G′}(𝔸_F)) = Nm(Z_{G′}(F))\Nm(Z_{G′}(𝔸_F)).
items.note: Tau Ceti's Class field theory Layer 13 plans the cyclic Hasse norm theorem (cyclicHasseNorm).

items.name: Proposition 9.5 (the linear relative trace formula)
items.statement: For ω a unitary central character and f ω-nice, 4 Σ_γ Orb^η_ω(f, γ) = Σ_π I_π(f) (9.1), the first sum over Z-regular semisimple γ ∈ H(F)\G(F)^{Z−rss}/Nm(Z_{G′}(F))H(F), the second over cuspidal π of G(𝔸_F) with central character ω_{i,j} for some (i, j).
items.note: Proof omitted as standard (Rogawski's analysis of K_{f,ω} [Rog83]; cf. [Zha14b, Theorem 2.3], [GH19, Theorem 18.2.2]); it uses the ⟨·,·⟩_Pet normalization.

items.name: Proposition 9.6 (the twisted relative trace formula)
items.statement: For ω′ = ω ∘ Nm unitary and f′ ω′-nice, (2L(1, η))² Σ_δ Orb_{ω′}(f′, δ) = Σ_Π J^{x,y}_Π(f′) (9.2), over Z-regular semisimple δ ∈ H′(F)\G′(F)^{Z−rss}/Z_{G′}(F)H′_{x,y}(F) and cuspidal Π of G′(𝔸_F) with central character ω′; here vol([Z_{H′_{x,y}}]) = (2L(1, η))² with L(s, η) completed.
items.note: The stabilizer of a Z-regular semisimple element is Z_{H′_{x,y}} by (7.9).

items.name: Global matching of orbital integrals
items.statement: If f = ⊗f_v and {f′_{x,y} = ⊗f′_{x,y,v}} (almost all zero) are local transfers at every place, then for matching global Z-regular semisimple γ ↔^{x,y} δ, the product formula ∏_v Ω_v(γ) = 1 (γ ∈ G(F)) gives Orb^η(f, γ) = Orb(f′_{x,y}, δ), and Orb^η_ω(f, γ) = Orb_{ω′}(f′_{x,y}, δ) (9.3) for ω unitary and ω′ = ω ∘ Nm.

items.name: Efficient transfers
items.statement: For ω, its base change ω′, a split place v_0 and a supercuspidal π_{v_0} of G(F_{v_0}), f and {f′_{x,y}} are efficient transfers for (ω, π_{v_0}) if they are ω- and ω′-nice, smooth transfers of each other, f_{v_0} is essentially a matrix coefficient of π_{v_0}, and f′_{x,y,v_0} is related to f_{v_0} as in Proposition 7.8 (so essentially a matrix coefficient of Π_{v_0} ≅ π_{v_0} ⊗ π_{v_0}).

items.name: Theorem 9.8 (Ramakrishnan: automorphic Chebotarev density)
items.statement: For E/F a quadratic extension of global fields, two cuspidal automorphic representations Π_1, Π_2 of Res_{E/F}GL_n(𝔸_F) are isomorphic iff Π_{1,v} ≅ Π_{2,v} for almost all places v of F split in E.
items.note: Cited from Ramakrishnan [Ram18].

items.name: Proposition 9.9 (comparison for a fixed unramified character)
items.statement: Fix unramified π^0_v at almost all split v and a supercuspidal π_{v_0} at a split place v_0. There is at most one cuspidal Π of G′(𝔸_F) such that, for all efficient transfers f, {f′_{x,y}} for (ω, π_{v_0}), (1/L(1, η)²) Σ_{x,y} J^{x,y}_Π(f′_{x,y}) = Σ_{π∈B(Π)} I_π(f), the right sum over cuspidal π with π_v ≅ π^0_v for almost all split v and π_{v_0} the fixed supercuspidal, Π = BC(π); B(Π) is the finite set of π with BC(π) = Π.
items.note: Uses the fundamental lemma (Theorem 7.12) at inert places, Proposition 7.8 at split places, Hecke-trace functionals ([Zha14b, proof of Proposition 2.10]), linear independence of Hecke characters ([Bad18, Appendix]) and Theorem 9.8.

items.name: Theorem 9.11 (global transfer of relative characters)
items.statement: Let E/F be a quadratic extension of number fields with every archimedean place split, (x, y) ∈ X_n × X_{n+1}, and Π cuspidal on G′ with central character ω′, Π ≅ Π^σ, and Π_{v_0} ≅ π_0 ⊗ π_0 supercuspidal at a split place v_0. For an ω′-nice factorizable f′ with f′_{v_0} essentially a matrix coefficient of Π_{v_0}, there is an ω-nice factorizable f matching {f′ at (x, y), 0 elsewhere}, with (f, {f′_{x′,y′}}) efficient for (ω, π_{v_0}), and (1/L(1, η)²) J^{x,y}_Π(f′) = Σ_{π∈B(Π)} I_π(f) (9.4). If the pairs (f′_v, f_v) match at each place, f may be chosen so that ∏_v J^{x,y,♮}_{Π_v}(f′_v) = ∏_v I^♮_{π_v}(f_v) (9.5) for π ∈ B(Π).
items.note: Proof: B(Π) = {π · η_{i,j}}, supports in G_v[x, y] (Lemma 7.11) give Σ I_{πη_{i,j}}(f) = 4I_π(f), and vol(E^×\𝔸^1_E)/L(1, η) = vol(F^×\𝔸^1_F).

items.name: Supercuspidal matrix coefficients and central projection
items.statement: For π supercuspidal with central character ω, every matrix coefficient lies in C_c^∞(Z_G(F)\G(F), ω), and f ↦ f_ω(g) = ∫_{Z_G(F)} f(gz)ω(z) dz maps C_c^∞(G(F)) onto C_c^∞(Z_G(F)\G(F), ω^{-1}).
items.note: SR.3 plans the matrix-coefficient criteria for supercuspidality.

items.name: Lemma 10.1 (nonvanishing Z-regular orbital integrals of supercuspidal matrix coefficients)
items.statement: For F nonarchimedean and π supercuspidal of G(F) with central character ω, there are a matrix coefficient Φ of π, f ∈ C_c^∞(G(F)) with f_ω = Φ, and a Z-regular semisimple γ with Orb_ω(f, γ) ≠ 0.
items.note: Uses Sakellaridis–Venkatesh [SV17, §6] for the strongly tempered pair: λ_π(W) = ∫_{H(F)} [W(π, h)W, Ŵ_0]_π dh for some W_0; Φ_0(g) = [W(π, g)W_0, Ŵ_0]_π; Ichino–Zhang [Zha14b, Appendix A] (convergence off a null set and nonvanishing on a set of positive measure; Theorem A.2).

items.name: Lemma 10.3 (relative character as an integral of orbital integrals)
items.statement: g ↦ Orb(Φ_0, g) = ∫_{H(F)}∫_{H(F)} Φ_0(h_1^{-1}gh_2) dh_1 dh_2 is locally L¹ on G(F), and I_π(f) = ∫_{G(F)} f(g) Orb(Φ_0, g) dg for f ∈ C_c^∞(G(F)).
items.note: Cited from [Zha14b, Lemma A.5].

items.name: Proposition 10.4 (local transfer of relative characters, split case)
items.statement: For E = F × F, U(V_n) ≅ {(g, g^θ)}, U(V_{n+1}) ≅ {(g, g^θ)} and J_Π = J^{w_n,w_{n+1}}_Π: for matching f_1 ⊗ f_2 ∈ C_c^∞(G(F) × G(F)) and f = f_1 ∗ f_2^{θ∨} and every irreducible π of G(F), J_{BC(π)}(f_1 ⊗ f_2) = I_π(f).

items.name: The unramified base change homomorphism of Hecke algebras
items.statement: For E/F unramified, BC : ℋ_{K′}(G′(F)) → ℋ_K(G(F)) is defined by Sat(BC(φ))(π) = Sat(φ)(BC(π)) for spherical π of G(F), and is injective; the Satake transform of §3.1 is related by evaluating Π = Π_n ⊠ Π_{n+1} at its Satake parameters (Remark 10.5).
items.note: ET.3–ET.4 plan the unramified Hecke-function transfers for cyclic base change.

items.name: Lemma 10.6 (unramified identity of relative characters)
items.statement: For E/F unramified, f′ ∈ ℋ_{K′}(G′(F)) and (x, y) ∈ G′(F) ∗ (w_n, w_{n+1}), J^{x,y,♮}_{BC(π)}(f′) = I^♮_π(BC(f′)) for every representation π of G(F).
items.note: Both sides vanish unless π is unramified, and then equal Sat(f′)(BC(π)) by the normalizations (8.1), (8.3), (8.7) on spherical Whittaker vectors.

items.name: Proposition 10.7 (weak local transfer of relative characters)
items.statement: Let E/F be a quadratic extension of number fields with all archimedean places split, Π = BC(π) cuspidal on G′(𝔸_F) and (x, y) such that J^{x,y}_Π(f′) ≠ 0 for some nice f′. For every non-split place v_0 there is C(Π_{v_0}, x, y) ∈ ℂ^×, depending only on (x, y) and Π_{v_0}, with J^{x,y,♮}_{Π_{v_0}}(f′_{v_0}) = C(Π_{v_0}, x, y) I^♮_{π_{v_0}}(f_{v_0}) for all matching f_{v_0} and {f′_{v_0} at (x, y), 0 elsewhere}.
items.note: From Theorem 9.11 and the factorizations (8.13), (8.14).

items.name: Corollary 10.8 (the constant is 1 at unramified places)
items.statement: In Proposition 10.7, if Π_{v_0} is unramified and (x, y) ∈ G′(F) ∗ (w_n, w_{n+1}), then C(Π_{v_0}, x, y) = 1.
items.note: Test on 1_{K′_{v_0}} and 1_{K_{v_0}} (Theorem 7.12) with Lemma 10.6.

items.name: Theorem 11.1 (base change fundamental lemma for the spherical Hecke algebra)
items.statement: Let E/F be an unramified extension of p-adic local fields. For any φ ∈ ℋ_{K′}(G′(F)), BC(φ) ∈ ℋ_K(G(F)) matches {φ_{x,y}} with φ_{x,y} = φ for (x, y) = (w_n, w_{n+1}) and 0 otherwise: for γ ∈ G(F)^rss with γ ↔^{w_n,w_{n+1}} δ, Ω(γ) Orb^η(BC(φ), γ) = Orb(φ, δ) (11.1), and Orb^η(BC(φ), γ) = 0 if γ ↔^{x,y} δ for (x, y) outside the G′(F)-orbit of (w_n, w_{n+1}).
items.note: The vanishing part is immediate from supp(BC(φ)) ⊂ G[w_n, w_{n+1}]; the identity is proved by globalizing and comparing the relative trace formulas.

items.name: Lemma 11.2 (reduction to Z-regular orbits and central characters)
items.statement: For E/F unramified p-adic and φ ∈ ℋ_{K′}(G′(F)), if Ω(γ) Orb^η_ω(BC(φ), γ) = Orb_{ω′}(φ, δ) (11.2) for every unitary central character ω (base change ω′) and matching Z-regular semisimple γ ↔^{w_n,w_{n+1}} δ, and Orb^η_ω(BC(φ), γ) = 0 when γ ↔^{x,y} δ for (x, y) outside the G′(F)-orbit of (w_n, w_{n+1}), then Theorem 11.1 holds.
items.note: Local constancy of orbital integrals [Zha14b, Lemma 3.12] on A′ = GL_{n+1}//GL_n ≅ X_{n+1}//U(V_n) ≅ 𝔸^{2n+1}, whose Z-regular locus is {a_1 ≠ 0, a_{2n+1} ≠ 0}, and Fourier inversion over the unramified characters of Nm(Z_{G′}(F))/Z_G(O_F).

items.name: Lemma 11.3 (approximation by global elements)
items.statement: Given matching Z-regular semisimple γ ↔^{w_n,w_{n+1}} δ at v_0 and the auxiliary data at split places v_cusp, v_reg, there are matching global Z-regular semisimple a ∈ G(F)^rss and b ∈ G′(F)^rss (for the globalized E/F) with the same local orbital integrals at v_cusp, v_reg and v_0: Orb_{ω′}(f′_{v_cusp}, b) = Orb^η_ω(f_{v_cusp}, a) ≠ 0, likewise at v_reg, Orb_{ω′}(φ, b) = Orb_{ω′}(φ, δ) and Ω(a) Orb^η_ω(BC(φ), a) = Ω(γ) Orb^η_ω(BC(φ), γ).
items.note: Density of G(F) in ∏_{v∈{v_0,v_cusp,v_reg}} G(F_v) and local constancy.

items.name: Proposition 11.4 (test functions isolating one orbit)
items.statement: (1) There are efficient matching f = ⊗f_v, f′ = ⊗f′_v for (ω, π_{v_cusp}) with I_ω(f) = Orb^η_ω(f, a) = Orb_{ω′}(f′, b) = (1/(4L(1, η)²)) J^{w_n,w_{n+1}}_{ω′}(f′) ≠ 0 (11.4). (2) f̂ = BC(φ) ⊗ ⊗_{v≠v_0} f_v and f̂′ = φ ⊗ ⊗_{v≠v_0} f′_v are nice, their orbital integrals vanish at every global matching pair in orbits other than a ↔ b, and I_ω(f̂) = Orb^η_ω(f̂, a), (1/(4L(1, η)²)) J^{w_n,w_{n+1}}_{ω′}(f̂′) = Orb_{ω′}(f̂′, b).
items.note: The auxiliary places S_aux cut out the finitely many other orbits by congruence conditions on the invariant polynomials c_i (G_v[l_v], G′_v[l_v]); the proof calls them invariants of H′(F_v) × H′(F_v) on G(F_v), where H(F_v) × H(F_v) is meant (sourceIssues E12).

items.name: Lemma 11.5 (unit orbital integrals and the center)
items.statement: For z ∈ Z_{G′}(F_v), Orb(1_{K′_v}, bz) ≠ 0 iff z ∈ Z_{G′}(O_v); hence for unramified unitary ω′_v, Orb_{ω′}(1_{K′_v}, b) = ∫_{Nm(Z_{G′}(O_v))} Orb(1_{K′_v}, bz) ω′_v(z) dz = Orb(1_{K′_v}, b) ≠ 0.

items.name: Hermitian spaces and self-dual lattices over a p-adic field
items.statement: Over a nonarchimedean local field there are exactly two isometry classes of nondegenerate n-dimensional Hermitian spaces (|𝒱_n| = 2), distinguished by η(det); for E/F unramified the split space V_n carries a self-dual lattice Λ_n, U(Λ_n) is hyperspecial, and any two self-dual lattices are U(V_n)-conjugate.
items.note: GN.2 plans local classification of quadratic and Hermitian forms and integral lattices (as for PAPER-LI-ZHANG-22-B/1).
